headline: Dry through Friday, then cooler weather with frost chances and showers returning Saturday.
summary: A low-pressure system dropping south just off the coast is the main driver of the pattern. Through Friday, mostly dry weather continues, with a weak front Thursday bringing clouds and a slight chance of showers in the south Sound and south interior. Friday turns clearer but cooler, with highs in the 50s. Saturday morning looks like the coldest of the stretch, with lows in the 30s and possible frost. Showers return from Saturday into next week, and snow levels may briefly drop to 3,000 to 4,000 feet. Forecasters don't expect significant impacts from the rain, and temperatures should warm slightly afterward. The weekend and next week remain uncertain because models disagree on whether the low stays put or moves away.
changes: Compared with the morning, the weekend turned cooler and showerier. Showers now run from Saturday into next week rather than a single weak system, and a frost chance and colder Saturday morning were added.
